objective: Standard statement: for the incidence graph B(H) of a connected 3-regular triple system H with distinct points per line that is not 2-colourable, prove (1) a splice lemma: if a graph A with a vertex x of degree 3 satisfies genus(A - x) = genus(A), then splicing A at x into any connected graph R at a vertex of degree 3, along any bijection of the three edges, has genus genus(A) + genus(R); without the hypothesis additivity fails (K3,3 with K3,3 has genus 1); (2) the Heawood graph satisfies the hypothesis and planar pieces add no genus, so genus(B(H)) is the number of Heawood braces when every other brace is planar, and the sum of the braces' genera when every non-planar brace satisfies the hypothesis at every vertex; (3) if both sides of a 3-edge splice satisfy the hypothesis, every minimum-genus embedding is a connected sum of minimum-genus embeddings of the two sides; in a three-fold space with planar glue both sides of every tight cut do, so every minimum-genus embedding is assembled from Heawood maps (one per Fano atom) and planar maps of the glue; (4) the Fano plane's space is the Heawood map, unique up to symmetry, whose dual is the 7-vertex triangulation of the torus with the gadget's triangles and contacts as its two colour classes. Nearest known result: Battle-Harary-Kodama-Youngs 1962; Decker-Glover-Huneke 1981; Stahl 1980; the Heawood map. Classification: to be decided.
status: Proved: splice lemma (a piece that keeps its genus when the splice vertex is deleted adds exactly its genus; fails for K3,3); the incidence graph of a three-fold space with planar glue has genus = number of Fano atoms (Heawood braces), plus the genus of rigid non-planar glue; all its minimum-genus embeddings are connected sums of Heawood maps and planar maps (count = product / 2 per cut); the Fano space is the chiral Heawood map, dual K7 on the torus with points and lines as the two colour classes.
title: Fano atoms are handles
